WORKLOG - task 1 of protection_claims_desk (Northbeam ShieldCare). Written as the task was designed and updated at every revision; every figure comes from the harness in section 11 and is re-checked by the gates in section 13.
1. STEP 0 DRAW (by code, before the tree or the computations were designed)
   .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/protection_claims_desk --task 1
   {"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/protection_claims_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 6, 4]}
   Three prerequisite problems and four computations carrying 5, 5, 6 and 4 factors. The 6 went to the claim excess (the widest rule: a base excess, a counting window, a frequency loading, a prompt-report reduction, a managed care allowance and an age adjustment); the 4 went to the instalment; the two 5s to the excess settlement and to the invoice settlement.
2. WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
   A business caller asks for one thing: the premium invoice on the fleet plan squared off before the quarter closes. The invoice figure is not on the account, because the period the plan has reached was never billed; and the premium may not be taken at all until a payment stands against the excess on a theft claim that was approved, replaced and paid weeks ago and never billed. So one request unfolds into four writes, two of them the customer's own. Every figure is a multi-factor calculation over a long reconciled history (nineteen instalments billed and settled, three claims, three payouts, a cover grant and a reinstatement) plus reads into three other product lines: the store credit account's terms, balance, limit, statements and last payment; the purchase orders' merchandise lines; and the managed care agreement's included visits and the visits drawn on it. The agent cannot guess its way there: the policies say what waits on what, and each number needs the right window, the right ladder and the right base.
3. SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, REMAINING
   Task 0 occupied protection_ext_premium_late_fee_scale, protection_ext_premium_arrears_settlement, protection_ext_claim_repair_settlement and protection_ext_spoilage_allowance with their four tools (bill_premium_late_fee_5ae6a6af, settle_premium_arrears_c5640f60, book_claim_payout_542e239c, book_spoilage_allowance_79e3e314). This task claims the remaining four policies and four tools: protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing / bill_premium_instalment_3dd4c03b (a premium charge of the instalment kind, where task 0 claimed the late-fee kind through a different tool), protection_ext_claim_excess_charge / bill_claim_deductible_d5a520f4, protection_ext_claim_excess_settlement / settle_claim_deductible_46d57fef (owner user) and protection_ext_fleet_invoice_settlement / settle_fleet_invoice_2818623b (owner user; task 0's premium payment was the arrears settlement on a household plan, this one is the invoice settlement on a business account). The two scopes are disjoint in policies, in tools and in (target_tool, computes) pairs, and with this task the difficulty's eight policies are fully covered, so nothing is reserved.
4. THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD
   Root: protection_ext_fleet_invoice_settlement, the premium invoice the caller asks about. Two branches meet at it:
     protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing -> root
     protection_ext_claim_excess_charge -> protection_ext_claim_excess_settlement -> root
   Edge 1 (root <- instalment), value_input, gate invoice_items, form state.
     Sentence in the root's own rule: 'The amount the account settles is fixed only after every premium period the plan has reached stands billed on it.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after'; (2) a record-visible state - a premium period standing billed on the plan - with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) the strength 'only after' and the scope 'every premium period the plan has reached' match the edge's condition exactly. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: bill_premium_instalment_3dd4c03b is the only tool that bills a premium period (the other premium-charge tool of the difficulty bills a late fee, which is not a period). Derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on every period reached standing billed; the records show instalment periods running from the tenth to the ninth and the most recent ending 2026-09-09, with nothing for the period beginning 2026-09-10; the instalment policy's own rule says what the instalment for a period comes to; so the period must be billed first. Seed evidence: the last charge's period_end is 2026-09-09 and premium_outstanding stands at nothing.
   Edge 2 (root <- excess settlement), state_gate, gate protection_events.deductible_amount, form state.
     Sentence: 'The premium on the plan is taken only once a payment against the claim excess stands received on the plan for every claim the plan has settled by replacement.' Four-point test: (1) 'only once'; (2) a record-visible state - a payment against the claim excess standing received on the plan, over the claims the plan has settled by replacement, which the settlement_basis on the decision rows makes readable; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) the strength and the scope are those of the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: settle_claim_deductible_46d57fef is the only tool that records a payment against an excess. The set is not empty and not vacuous: the plan carries exactly one claim settled by replacement, the decision of 2026-08-12 on SC-2026-70431 whose settlement_basis is replacement, whose replacement was paid on 2026-08-14, and against that claim the history carries no excess payment of any kind and the plan's outstanding excess figure stands at nothing. The state is therefore FALSE at frozen_time, on rows the agent reads. Derivation: the sentence says the premium waits on a payment standing against the excess of every replacement-settled claim; the records show one such claim and no such payment; the settlement policy's own rule says what the account settles on a claim excess, and its own prerequisite sentence says that is fixed only after the excess stands billed; so the excess must be billed and then settled by the customer before the premium is taken. The scope is replacement-settled claims and not claims at large because a claim settled by repair carries no excess at all on a plan that waives it on a repair, which this plan does - the two earlier claims on this plan are exactly that case.
   Edge 3 (excess settlement <- excess charge), value_input, gate owed_measure, form state.
     Sentence: 'What the account settles on a claim excess is fixed only after that excess stands billed on the plan.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after'; (2) a record-visible state - the excess standing billed on the plan; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) exactly the scope of the condition. Exactly one write brings it about: bill_claim_deductible_d5a520f4. Derivation: the decision of 2026-08-12 approved the claim by replacement and the replacement was paid on 2026-08-14; this plan waives its excess only on a claim settled by repair, so an excess is owed; the ledger carries none; the excess-charge policy's own rule says what that excess comes to; so it must be billed first. Seed evidence: the decision row's settlement_basis is replacement and deductible_outstanding is nothing.
   Topological order: instalment, excess charge, excess settlement, invoice settlement - the gold writes at actions 12, 14, 16 and 18. The two branches may be taken either way round and commute; the proof is in prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness (both orders give the root 136.54 and the same terminal hash, because the instalment touches only the premium account and the excess pair only the deductible account). Per-edge deletion sensitivity: skip the instalment and the invoice moves 136.54 -> 129.66; skip the excess charge and the settlement moves 127.50 -> 72.00; skip the settlement and no payment stands against the excess billed, so the premium may not be taken and the terminal state differs by the payment entry and by the outstanding excess (202.50 instead of 75.00). user_scenario names no prerequisite problem and no tool validates one; see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint and tools_do_not_block.
5. THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD (per exact write subject, at handling time)
   protection_premium_charge (the instalment) and protection_premium_payment (the invoice settlement) are governed by protection_premium_billing, whose billable_plan_state gate - 'Premium is billed, and premium payments applied, only while the plan stands in application_received, active or claim_hold' - holds because the plan stands active; authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key protection_plans.plan_id bound to the plan_id argument. protection_combo_membership_interaction governs the charge too and has no structured gate: its scope is inherited as policy_scope, and it is what says a business fleet plan takes its pricing from the contract price book with no membership discount at all - which is why nothing in the instalment reads a membership (this profile holds none).
   protection_deductible_charge is governed by protection_claim_settlement, whose payable_plan_state gate - 'A payout is booked only while the plan stands active or in claim_hold' - applies to the excess charge as well as to a payout and holds on an active plan. protection_deductible_payment is governed by the same policy, but no gate of it applies to that subject, so its scope is inherited as policy_scope.
   Time gates: none of the four writes is governed by a base eligibility of kind time, so temporal_feasibility is empty by construction. The clocks that do bite are checked by hand. The claim report window is ninety calendar days from the incident day, day zero inclusive, anchored on protection_events.incident_date: the theft of 2026-07-28 was reported on 2026-08-03, day six, comfortably inside; it would just hold at a report on 2026-10-26 (day ninety) and just fail at 2026-10-27 (day ninety-one). The premium grace clock is forty-five calendar days from the first day of the unpaid period: the period billed on this call begins 2026-09-10, six days before the handling day, so grace has not run and no late fee is owed - which is why this task carries no late-fee obligation even though the difficulty has a policy for one.
6. THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
   Target object: the one ShieldCare Business Fleet Protection plan on the profile, initial_state.protection_plans.a4c4c25e-dec2-4e4a-a8bf-92e8f129e72d, covering the laptop with serial NBLT9920-7714503. Correlation keys: plan_id for every premium, cover and excess row; claim_reference for every claim row; covered_item_serial for the machine. The claim being settled is SC-2026-70431 and no other: it is the only claim approved by replacement, the only one whose settlement was not a repair, and therefore the only one that carries an excess at all - the two earlier claims (SC-2025-64218 and SC-2026-20977) were settled by repair, and this plan waives its excess on a repair, which is why no excess entry stands against them. Rows entering each aggregate: the nineteen instalment charges and nineteen payments (the invoice), the cover grant and the reinstatement (the cover), the three payouts and three claim files (the loading and the frequency), the claim file and decision and payout of SC-2026-70431 (the base excess, the report promptness and the billing delay). Rows excluded: the purchase order of 2025-11-12 falls inside a twelve-month window but outside a three-month one, which is what the trading window turns on; the claim of 2025-08-18 falls inside the whole term but outside the eight months counted from the reinstatement, which is what the frequency loading turns on. The excess charge and its payment both carry claim_reference into the new rows, so the derived entries are tied to the source claim and not to the customer alone.
7. WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS (and what changes if it is removed)
   customers: the business profile, with the registered name that finds it and the two credentials the check matches. protection_plans: the holding; its coverage_end_date decides the periods billed in advance, its covered_item_purchase_date the age adjustment on the excess, and its recorded premium and excess figures are both accurate here (this task carries no stale cache; its trap is a missing entry, not a wrong total). The nineteen instalment charges and their nineteen payments: they are what make the invoice carry exactly the one unbilled period, and they are why nothing stood outstanding before the call; remove one payment and the invoice figure moves. The cover grant and the reinstatement of 2026-02-10: the reinstatement is what makes the claims that load the excess be counted over eight months rather than the whole term - remove it and the loading rises from thirty-five to seventy-five dollars. The three claims with their decisions and payouts: the two repairs put the repair tally at the plan's figure of two, which is why the third approval had to be a replacement and therefore carries an excess at all; the payouts of 1120.00 and 1480.00 are what carry the twelve-month total over two thousand five hundred and so set the instalment's loading at fifteen percent. The three claim intakes: the police report on the theft intake is what the plan requires before a theft claim is adjudicated, and it is read by the prompt-report tier. credit_accounts and credit_events: the account's net thirty terms, its balance against its limit, the statement closed on 2026-08-31 and the payment of 2026-08-28 decide the share due straight away, the handling charge, the trading window, the terms discount, the entries the invoice carries and the prompt-payment discount; remove the August statement and both the trading window and the invoice entries fall to their fall-through tiers. purchase_orders and order_events: the three merchandise lines are the trading record; the 2025-11-12 line is the near-miss that only a twelve-month window picks up. service_agreements and service_events: the managed care agreement's twelve included visits and the two visits drawn are what earn the sixty-dollar allowance on the excess; remove the drawn visits and it falls to thirty.
   Automatic-clause check: the next anniversary is 2027-02-10, so no reinstatement is due; the term runs to 2028-02-09, so no expiry; grace has not run on any period, so no late fee and no termination for non-payment; the excesses on the two repairs are waived by the plan itself, so no excess is owed on them. Nothing in the seed lights an obligation this task does not discharge.
8. THE PERSONA (design)
   Nadia Gildersleeve is the office manager of a forty-strong instrument shop, brisk and numerate, working against a quarter-end; her register is the opposite of task 0's unhurried piano teacher, and the text is organised as she would talk - the deadline and the single request first, then flat factual answers, then reactions. Volunteered at the opening: the quarter-end, the one request (the premium invoice on the plan squared off today, on the account) and the authorisation boundary (she will be told the figure and will put the payment through herself; the desk may do whatever else the plan needs). Given only when asked: the registered name, the account number 3122860714, the card last four 2745, the postal code 60622, the serial from the asset register, the claim number, the two dates of the theft, and the answer that the business carries no separate cover on the laptops. Reacted to only after the desk says something: the excess never having been billed (she is resigned, blames two different people, and settles it herself on the invoice account), a figure for the excess that strikes her as steep (she asks once for it to be read out, then accepts it), and the premium figure (she puts that through too). Her last reaction answers the last gold action - the premium taken and the invoice square - and she rings off there. She names no document to send, no address and no further work, so nothing she says lies outside gold; and she never mentions an excess, an unbilled period or a deductible before the desk raises it.
9. DEPTH AND BREADTH
   Depth: the invoice figure waits on the period reached being billed, and the premium may be taken only once a payment stands against the excess of the replacement-settled claim, which in turn waits on the excess being billed at all - three hops from the surface request, two of them ending in a handover to the customer. Breadth per computation: the instalment reads the protection payout and claim history, the credit account's statements and terms, and the orders ledger; the excess reads the claim's peril, its payout, the reinstatement entry, the claim file count, the intake documents, the item purchase day and the service agreement's included visits and drawn visits; the excess settlement reads the deductible ledger both ways, the credit account's terms, balance, limit and purchase-order rule, and three different date anchors on the claim; the invoice settlement reads the whole premium ledger, the credit account's statements, terms and last payment, and the instalment just billed. Negative space: no late fee (grace has not run), no excess on the two repairs (the plan waives it), no membership discount (a fleet plan takes none), and no refund of any kind.
10. WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES IT
   (a) Reading the plan's premium outstanding (nothing, before the instalment is billed) as the invoice: the rule carries the plan's monthly premium only where the premium billed does not exceed the premium received. (b) Billing the instalment at the plan's 39.00: the loading and the two discounts combine to one hundred and six percent. (c) Applying the loading and discounts one after another instead of combining them once: the rule says outright that they are combined into one rate and the premium adjusted once. (d) Reading the trading record over three months: that drops two of the three orders and the discount with them. (e) Counting the claims that load the excess over the whole term: that pulls in the August 2025 claim and raises the loading to seventy-five dollars. (f) Taking the excess as the plan's 125.00 deductible: theft with a settlement above ten times the deductible doubles it. (g) Taking the whole excess now: the account's terms and its balance against its limit put sixty percent due straight away. (h) Counting the billing delay from the day the claim was decided: on a plan whose claims are worked ahead of the queue it runs from the day the replacement was paid, which is thirty-three days and not forty-four, and that moves the deferred part from twenty-four to twelve dollars. (i) Discounting the invoice-raising charge with the rest: the rule says it is added after the discount.
11. THE STANDARD SOLUTION AND THE EXECUTED RECALCULATION
   Read: the profile by the registered name; verify on two details; the plan; the whole protection ledger; the claim intakes; the credit account and its entries; the purchase orders and their line charges; the service agreement and its visits. Then write, in the order the prerequisite sentences entail: the instalment (41.34), the excess (202.50), the customer's settlement of the excess (127.50, through a handover) and the customer's settlement of the premium invoice (136.54, through a second handover).
   Harness actually executed (scratch script importing the gate's own evaluator and the real tools, replaying each write onto the seeded DB and evaluating each policy on the world standing just before its own write):
     protection_ext_fleet_instalment_billing: result=41.34 (bindings 12, branches 12, history rows 4); factor baselines 43.68 / 43.68 / 35.49 / 42.51; all-baseline 39.0
     protection_ext_claim_excess_charge: result=202.5 (18, 15, 8); 77.5 / 242.5 / 167.5 / 225.0 / 262.5 / 242.5; all-baseline 165.0
     protection_ext_claim_excess_settlement: result=127.5 (17, 15, 10); 72.0 / 208.5 / 109.5 / 115.5 / 139.5; all-baseline 125.0
     protection_ext_fleet_invoice_settlement: result=136.54 (18, 16, 39); 134.25 / 139.02 / 55.51 / 131.95 / 121.54; all-baseline 39.0
     prerequisite sensitivity: the invoice without the instalment 129.66; the excess settlement without the excess charge 72.0; the root with the excess branch taken first 136.54, terminal hash 9a72a4713e1a91dd37c9581c4852f910a986f5ddbc0f2299f96b15c2b295ad02 in both orders
   Those are exactly the expected values, the baseline_result figures and the factor_sensitivity entries in computations, and check_compute recomputes each at handling time.
12. RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP (per policy)
   Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses, crosses a category, caps or rounds quotes its rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis, each ladder binding quoting the whole tier sentence. Reverse, policy by policy. Instalment: the window ladder -> statements_3m / account_active / trading_window_months; the trading ladder -> merch_spend / volume_discount_pct; the loading ladder -> payouts_12m / claims_12m / claims_loading_pct; the terms ladder -> terms_days / returned_payments_12m / terms_discount_pct; the combined-rate sentence -> result. Excess: the base ladder -> peril / claim_settled / base_excess; the counting ladder -> latest_reinstatement / loading_window_months; the frequency ladder -> claims_in_window / frequency_loading; the prompt ladder -> incident_date / report_date / days_to_report / police_report_on_file / prompt_report_reduction; the care ladder -> care_visits / care_visits_drawn / care_allowance; the age ladder -> item_age_at_loss / age_adjustment; the sum sentence -> result. Excess settlement: the owed ladder -> ded_billed / ded_paid / latest_excess / prior_excess_payments_12m / owed_measure; the share ladder -> terms_days / acct_balance / acct_limit / share_due_now_pct; the handling ladder -> po_required / handling_charge; the delay ladder -> payout_date / decision_date / billing_delay_days; the deferral ladder -> loss_report_date / deferred_amount; the take sentence -> result. Invoice settlement: the entries ladder -> prem_billed / prem_paid / statements_3m / invoice_items; the discount ladder -> terms_days / last_payment_days / prompt_discount_pct; the periods ladder -> po_required / months_of_cover_left / advance_periods; the pricing ladder -> latest_instalment / instalments_3m_total / instalments_3m_count / advance_price; the charge ladder -> premium_payments_1m / admin_charge; the ordering sentence ('the discount acts once on the total ... and the charge for raising the invoice is added after it rather than discounted with it') -> invoice_base and result. Sensitive words cross-checked: every 'last three months', 'last twelve months', 'last month' or 'window read' has a within_months; every 'no more than' or 'whichever is lower' has an MN; every 'taken to the cent' an RND; every 'never below nothing' an MX; every compound 'where ... and ...' a ternary whose test combines the two reads.
   Declared overwrites (two). The instalment policy supersedes protection_premium_billing's clause 'an instalment plan bills the monthly premium of the plan on the same day of each month' with its combined-rate sentence, because base and extended give different figures for the same quantity on this world (39.00 against 41.34). The excess policy supersedes protection_claim_settlement's clause 'The plan's deductible is billed once per approved claim' with its own sentence, because the excess billed is no longer the bare deductible (125.00 against 202.50) while remaining billed once for that claim. The waiver on a repair is inherited AND implemented: the excess policy's rule now states that no excess is billed on a claim the plan settles by repair where the plan waives its excess on a repair, and claim_settlement_basis and excess_waived carry it in compute - on this claim the decision records replacement, so the waiver does not engage and 202.50 stands, while on either of this plan's two repair-settled claims the same formula gives nothing, which is why neither carries an excess row. Nothing else diverges: the per-claim limit, the cover ceiling, the settlement method and the order in which the caps apply are all inherited unchanged, and the two writes that move the deductible account never touch the cover pool.
13. GATES RUN, AND THE CLOSURES
   check_extended --task 1: EXTENDED OK. check_task_tools: TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (8 tools). replay_tasks --task 1: REPLAY OK (19 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 70 = seeded 70). check_solvability --task 1: SOLVABILITY OK (4 calls, 5 base gates, 50 seed rows). check_compute --task 1: COMPUTE OK (4 computations, 20 factors, 9 cross-difficulty, 61 history rows, 60 branches). check_grounding --task 1: GROUNDING OK. check_cross_fire --task 1: SCOPE OK.
   Revision log. (i) Symptom: the first draft made the root's second prerequisite 'only once no claim excess stands unsettled against it'. Root cause: the customer settles only the share due straight away, so 75.00 of the excess still stands after her payment and the condition could never hold. Change: the sentence, the condition and the effect were reworded to wait on a payment standing received against every excess billed, which is exactly what that write brings about; the gate field moved to protection_events.deductible_amount. Re-run: EXTENDED OK and the closure recomputed. (ii) Symptom: check_compute reported that the excess settlement's history was not load-bearing - zeroing the aggregates left 127.50 unchanged, because the middle tier read the most recent excess through LATEST, which the test does not zero, and that happened to equal the sum. Root cause: two tiers coincided on this world. Change: the owed-measure ladder now turns on whether an excess payment stands on the plan inside the last twelve months, so zeroing the aggregates falls through to the plan's own deductible figure; and the handling charge, which had leaned on the same prior-payment count, was re-based on whether the excess owed is above the plan's deductible figure, which also removed a condition repeated between two factors. Re-run: COMPUTE OK; the declared baseline for that factor moved from 81.00 to 72.00 and the edge's load-bearing note and flips_to_true_by were updated in the same pass.
   Policy -> GT closure: each policy computes one argument of one call - instalment_amount at action 12, deductible_amount at 14, settlement_amount at 16 and settlement_amount at 18 - and charter_scope.extended_policies, required_documents and the computations' policy ids are the same four ids in the same order. Terminal state: one instalment entry of 41.34 with premium_outstanding at 41.34; one excess entry of 202.50 with deductible_outstanding at 202.50; one excess payment of 127.50 leaving 75.00 owed; one premium payment of 136.54 leaving premium_outstanding at -95.20, the surplus held against the two periods billed in advance exactly as base provides. Across the difficulty the two tasks now cover all eight extended policies with disjoint scopes.
14. DRAFT RECALCULATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE
   With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this worklog masked, and only the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, what the share tools return and the caller's own lines in view: she wants the premium invoice squared off; the invoice rule says the amount is fixed only after every period reached stands billed, and the ledger shows the last period ending 2026-09-09, so the period from 2026-09-10 must be billed first; the same rule says the premium is taken only once a payment stands against every excess billed, and the claim approved by replacement carries no excess, so the excess must be billed and then settled by the customer; the excess-settlement rule says what she settles is fixed only after the excess stands billed. Working forward: instalment 39.00 at one hundred and six percent = 41.34; excess 250.00 + 35.00 - 22.50 - 60.00 = 202.50; settlement 202.50 at sixty percent + 18.00 - 12.00 = 127.50; invoice (41.34 + two at 41.34) less two percent, plus 15.00 = 136.54. The draft agrees with gold on the conclusion, the object (the fleet plan on serial NBLT9920-7714503 and claim SC-2026-70431), the write sequence and every parameter, and no second reading of the published prose gave a different figure.
15. REVISION LOG, ROUND 2 (source-layer audit of 2026-09-18, items closed by id)
   F-08 / T1-01 (RED, closed by change): the root's second prerequisite sentence was universally quantified over the excesses already billed, a set this world leaves empty, so it gated nothing and the excess branch dropped out of the tree. The sentence now reads: The premium on the plan is taken only once a payment against the claim excess stands received on the plan for every claim the plan has settled by replacement. The quantifier runs over a set the records make non-empty by a seeded row - the decision of 2026-08-12 whose settlement_basis is replacement - while the plan carries no excess payment of any kind, so the state is false at frozen_time on the world rather than false only after some other write. The edge's condition, its unresolved_at_frozen_time (why_false, evidence, flips_to_true_by) and its load-bearing note were rewritten to that state, and the short path no longer follows from the policy: an agent that bills the reached period and takes the invoice has taken the premium while the replacement-settled claim's excess stands with nothing against it, which the root's own rule forbids. The scope is replacement-settled claims because a repair-settled claim on a waiving plan carries no excess at all, so the sentence blocks nothing on a plan that owes nothing. Numbers unchanged: 41.34, 202.50, 127.50 and 136.54, with the same four whole-baseline figures and the same twenty factor sensitivities.
   F-03 / T1-04 (RED, closed by change): the deductible waiver on a repair was inherited but implemented nowhere. The excess policy's rule and baseline now carry 'No excess is billed on a claim the plan settles by repair where the plan waives its excess on a repair, and the excess billed on such a claim is nothing', and compute carries it in claim_settlement_basis and excess_waived. The overwrite stays scoped to the billed-once clause it always named. On this claim the decision records replacement, so the waiver does not engage and 202.50 is unchanged; on either repair-settled claim of this plan the same formula now gives nothing, which is what base gives.
   F-05 (closed by change): the delay in billing now states its closing anchor - 'The delay in billing is counted to the day the excess stands billed on the plan' - and compute reads that day from the excess entry itself (excess_billed_day) rather than leaving NOW to be inferred. On this world the entry is booked at frozen_time, so thirty-three days and 127.50 are unchanged.
   F-11 (RED, closed by change): the promptness ladder no longer penalises the faster reporter. The police-report conjunct left the top tier (a police report is required only for theft, so a non-theft loss reported on day two fell through to nothing while the same loss reported on day five earned 22.50), and the binding that read the intakes went with it. The ladder is now monotone in promptness: inside three days fifty dollars, more than three and no more than seven 22.50, otherwise nothing. This claim reports on day six and still takes 22.50, so 202.50 is unchanged. The police report is still what base requires before a theft claim is adjudicated, and the intake read at action 4 is what shows it on file.
   F-01 (closed by change, observation side): the instalment overwrite was narrowed to 'an instalment plan bills the monthly premium of the plan', so base's billing-day provision and its month-end fallback stay in force and fix the period this entry is stamped with; the records leave exactly one period reached and unbilled, 2026-09-10 to 2026-10-09.

user_scenario:
Nadia Gildersleeve runs the office side of Marlowe Instrument Works, a forty-strong instrument shop on the west side of Chicago, and she is the one who signs off the invoices. She is brisk, numerate and slightly impatient: the quarter closes at the end of the month, her accountant wants every supplier account clean, and the ShieldCare cover on the workshop laptops is the last line she has not been able to tie off. What she says she wants is exactly that and nothing more: the premium invoice on the plan squared off today, on the account, so the ledger is straight before quarter end. She will not guess at figures; she wants the desk to tell her what the invoice comes to and she will put the payment through herself, and she says plainly that she is happy to authorise anything else the desk needs to do on the plan while she is on the line.

She gives details flatly and only when they are asked for. The number on the account is 3122860714. If a second thing on file is wanted she reads out the last four digits of the card the account is billed to, 2745; if a third is wanted she gives the postal code of the workshop, 60622. The registered name is Marlowe Instrument Works and she will spell it if asked. She does not know the customer number. If she is asked for the serial of the machine that went, she reads it from the asset register: NBLT9920-7714503, and she has the claim number in the same sheet: SC-2026-70431. Asked about that loss she says a laptop was taken out of a van outside a client site on the twenty-eighth of July, that she reported it on the third of August once the police report came through, and that the replacement machine arrived weeks ago. Asked whether anyone else has paid for it she says no, the business carries no separate cover on the laptops.

She reacts to what she is told rather than anticipating it. If the desk tells her the excess on that theft claim was never billed and has to be settled before the premium can be taken, she is more resigned than cross and says that figures, the whole thing was handled by two different people; she will put the excess through herself on the invoice account as soon as she is told the amount and handed the means to do it. If the desk tells her a figure for the excess that strikes her as high she says once that it sounds steep for a machine that cost under two thousand, and asks them to read out how it is made up, then accepts what she is told. When she is given the premium figure she puts that through on the invoice account too. She will not chase anything she has not been told about, and she never asks whether something else is owed.

When the desk confirms that the premium has been taken and the plan's invoice stands square, she says good, that is the last of them, and rings off. If she is asked anything about what the plan allows or how a figure is arrived at, she has no view of her own and says the desk knows its own rules better than she does.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The root problem waits on two branches: the instalment on the one hand and, on the other, the excess billed and then settled. Within the second branch the order is forced, since the settlement is fixed only after the excess stands billed. Between the branches either order is legal, and they commute: the instalment write touches only the premium account (a premium charge entry and premium_outstanding) while the excess write and its settlement touch only the deductible account (deductible entries and deductible_outstanding), and neither of those two computations reads a premium figure while the instalment's computation reads no deductible figure. Run in the gold order (instalment, excess, settlement) the root computes 136.54; run with the excess branch first and the instalment third it computes 136.54 again, and the terminal DB hash is the same in both runs (9a72a4713e1a91dd37c9581c4852f910a986f5ddbc0f2299f96b15c2b295ad02), because the four writes create four distinct rows and adjust two independent running figures.
